title: Notification on the phone
summary: Turns a content-free push into a notification: the iOS notification service extension or the Android push handler fetches the event, decrypts it on the phone, and shows the sender, the chat and the text. A tap opens the chat; the person can reply or mark as read from the notification.

accountUserId.description: Immutable Matrix ID resolved on this phone from the receiving pusher’s random account route. Never inferred from the current UI account or a mutable registration slot.

roomId.description: The chat within accountUserId. Grouping, suppression and clearing use the account and chat together.

kind.description: message: a decrypted event. chatRequest: an invite to a DM. groupInvite: an invite to a group. fallback: the event could not be fetched or decrypted in time.

title.description: DM: the other person's name. Group: the group name.

senderName.description: Group messages: the sender name, shown before the text.

body.description: The plain text of the message, the media label, or the invite or fallback string.

avatarUrl.description: Sender avatar in a DM, group avatar in a group.

isNoisy.description: From the push rules: true plays the sound of notification-settings. false in a group: no sound and, on iOS, interruptionLevel passive (ADR 0254). A plain group message under the quiet default has no notify action after decryption, so the SDK returns eventFilteredOut with no item: Android shows nothing, and iOS gives back empty content.

accountRoute.description: Opaque registration-lifetime code retained in local notification metadata and every open/reply/read action. Removed at sign-out; an old action cannot revive after the same Matrix account is added again.

notification.description: What the phone shows. Missing when the event must not show (see notes).

accountRoute.description: Random opaque code bound to the registering account on this phone. The provider does not receive the Matrix account ID.

unreadCount.description: From the push, for the app icon badge.

pushReceived.effect: Resolves accountRoute to exactly one local accountUserId, opens only that account in the extension or handler, fetches and decrypts the event, and retains its owner in each local notification and action. An unknown, ambiguous or missing route never falls back to another account.

open.effect: Tap: selects the notification owner after app lock and restore. message opens its joined chat; chatRequest opens that account’s requests box; groupInvite opens Groups with its invitations visible. A fallback or unknown kind opens the owner’s conversation list without entering or marking an unverified room. Event focus remains subject to chat-timeline support.

reply.effect: Uses only accountUserId to send the text as a reply to eventId and mark that account’s chat as read, without switching the UI account. A failure retains the same owner in the failure notification.

markAsRead.effect: Uses only accountUserId to send a public read receipt, then removes only that account’s notifications for roomId. An unavailable owner performs no write.

notes: Mac (bipe-chat/bipe#1223, ADR 0266). The Mac has no push: local notifications come from its own sync, one per chat per account, with the newest message. App running, window open: a new incoming unread message alerts by the room mode (the room rule, else the DM default, else the plain group default; quiet alerts only on a new mention). An open chat in the key window of the active app has none. Last window closed: the same, because the app keeps syncing; a click opens the window again. After quit: nothing shows, and the next launch does not alert for history; the list and the Dock badge show it. Screen locked, Mac awake: the same as a closed window, and the system decides what the lock screen shows. Asleep: nothing shows. After wake: sync starts again, and each room with new unread messages alerts once. The Dock badge adds the tab attention of every account (unread DMs and group mentions). A click selects the owner account and opens its chat, or its requests box for a chatRequest; an unknown owner opens only the app. No scam card, as above.

iOS runs this in the notification service extension with NotificationProcessSetup MultipleProcesses: the extension and the app share the SDK store in the app group, and the extension has little memory. Android runs it in the app process with SingleProcess and the app's sync service.

The extension never makes an SDK store. When the account's store folder is missing or empty (the app was deleted, the keychain kept the saved session), it shows the push without content and leaves the account to the app, which signs in again with a new device (account-start). A saved session restored into a new store makes a second encryption identity for the old device ID: the server keeps the old one-time keys, every key upload fails with 'One time key already exists', and new contacts cannot send this device keys (bipe#854). The app deletes the saved session before it deletes the store and signs in.

NotificationStatus: Event shows the item. EventFilteredOut, EventRedacted and EventNotFound show nothing (iOS: the extension delivers an empty notification so iOS does not show the gateway alert). An error or a timeout shows kind fallback: title bipe_app_name, body bipe_app_notification_new_message.
Undecryptable events: kind fallback. The text never shows as an error in a notification.

Invites: NotificationEvent.Invite in a DM is chatRequest (bipe_app_notification_chat_request with the sender name); in a group, groupInvite (bipe_group_notification_room_invite_body_with_sender). Requests open the requests box of #557.
DM name and photo follow ADR 0141: the other person, never the room name. RoomInfo isDm decides; NotificationRoomInfo.isDm gives it here.

Body: plain text, cut by the system. Photos, videos, files, voice messages and stickers use the existing timeline kind label. A nonblank attachment caption follows its kind label; raw filenames and media URLs are never used as a substitute caption. The extension/handler never downloads an attachment to make a preview. Text, emote and notice use their nonblank plain body. Unsupported or undecryptable content remains generic fallback. No Markdown or scam card (the card shows in chat, scam-warning).

Android channels: bipe_app_notification_channel_messages for messages, bipe_notifications_invites for requests and invites, one of each per account, in one channel group per account (bipe-chat/bipe#512, ADR 0138 rule 4). The group name is bipe_notifications_account_group with the account name, so Do Not Disturb and modes can allow one account and silence the other. Channel and group IDs carry a digest of the Matrix ID, never the ID. A push without an owner uses one ungrouped messages channel. Signing an account out deletes its group and channels. Each chat is one conversation notification with its messages; a group shows each sender name.

iOS Focus filter (bipe-chat/bipe#512): a SetFocusFilterIntent, title bipe_focus_filter_title, description bipe_focus_filter_description, parameter bipe_focus_filter_accounts (the accounts on this phone; none chosen shows bipe_focus_filter_all). Every notification sets filterCriteria to its accountUserId; the filter gives the system a predicate over the chosen accounts, and the system hides the others in that Focus. The choice stays on the phone.
Inline reply failure: bipe_dm_inline_reply_failed in a DM, bipe_group_notification_inline_reply_failed in a group.
Opening the chat, a read on another device, or markAsRead removes that chat's notifications. The badge follows the unread count of the chat list.
Nothing from a notification leaves the phone except the reply and the read receipt. No analytics (plan section 2).
App lock (ADR 0137) does not change notification content; a preview setting needs its own decision.

Every open, reply, mark-read, fallback and inline-reply failure retains accountUserId and roomId. Android PendingIntent identity includes account, room and action; notification tags and iOS thread identifiers use an opaque account-plus-room digest. Two accounts in the same group never share notification history, suppression or clearing.

A legacy or malformed push without a resolvable immutable account route shows only the generic new-message fallback, with no room route or reply/read actions. Do not decrypt with the current account, the last registered account, or the only saved account. A payload for a signed-out owner never opens or writes as another account.

Notification-client caches are scoped to the owning session. Sign-out detaches that account from action routing. Late work checks that the same session is still registered before showing, clearing or writing.

APNs pusher default_payload carries a random account_route alongside aps. Only the phone stores the route-to-Matrix-ID map; the provider gets no Matrix account ID. The route survives restarts and account switches, is removed on sign-out and is replaced if that account is added again. Re-register older native pushers once. The future Android transport must resolve an immutable registered route locally before it supplies the owning session; provider setup and delivery acceptance remain separate gates.

Local actions revalidate the stored registration-lifetime route before and after awaiting account restore, and before each SDK write. The same Matrix ID after sign-out is a new lifetime; old PendingIntents and delivered iOS actions must fail closed. Both native clients keep the local route map across process restart and clear only the signed-out owner’s routes.

Each generated local notification preserves its kind in the owner-bound payload. Tap routing uses that kind and consumes the pending route only in the restored owner’s view. Requests and group invites do not open an unjoined timeline or send a read receipt. Opening an invite destination shows the existing accept/decline controls; it never accepts automatically.

Quiet groups without the filtering entitlement (ADR 0254, bipe-chat/bipe#1079): the iOS pusher default_payload has aps interruption-level passive, so a gateway alert never rings. iOS shows that alert when the extension cannot run, and it may show it for empty content, because only Apple's filtering entitlement can drop a notification. What the extension shows sets its own level. A mention, a reply to the person and a new poll are noisy and alert as usual. Changing the payload bumps the registration ownerVersion, so existing pushers register again.

Per account (bipe-chat/bipe#511): the notification takes the owning account's sound and preview. preview false: title bipe_app_name, body bipe_app_notification_new_message, no sender. A company account with work-hours enabled and isWithinWorkHours false: no sound, iOS interruptionLevel passive, Android a silent notification (no sound, no vibration, no heads-up); it stays in the list. Another account's pushes are not affected.

Kind deviceApproval (bipe-chat/bipe#628, spec device-verification): bipe-api sends it through Sygnal with bipe_push_kind device_approval in the default_payload and the fixed event_id $device_approval (APNs format event_id_only needs an event ID), without room_id. The phone resolves account_route as for any push, fetches nothing and shows title bipe_app_verify_incoming_title and body bipe_app_verify_nudge_body. An unknown or missing route shows nothing. Tap: opens the owner account to its conversation list; the sync delivers the verification request and device-verification shows phase incoming. No reply or mark-read action.

Kinds recoveryStarted and recoveryCompleted (bipe-chat/bipe#171, spec recovery-alert): bipe-api sends them through Sygnal like deviceApproval, with bipe_push_kind recovery_started or recovery_completed in the default_payload and the fixed event_id $recovery_started or $recovery_completed, without room_id and without content (no method, no time, no device name). recovery_started goes to every Bipe Next pusher of the account when a recovery or a PIN reset starts (email, apple, google; guardian when it is built). recovery_completed goes to every Bipe Next pusher of the account when a claim completes a recovery or the synced token signs in a new device; the new device has no pusher yet. The phone resolves account_route as for any push and fetches nothing. recoveryStarted: title bipe_recovery_alert_title, body bipe_recovery_push_started_body. recoveryCompleted: title bipe_app_name, body bipe_recovery_push_completed_body. Sound as for deviceApproval. An unknown or missing route shows nothing. Tap: opens the owner account and runs recovery-alert check at once (GET /v1/me/account). When the push arrives while the app is open, the app runs that check at once too, and shows the banner. No reply or mark-read action.

Sender photo (bipe-chat/bipe#771). iOS: a message notification is a communication notification. The service builds an INPerson for the sender (display name, the avatar thumbnail at most 3 s, handle and custom ID the Matrix ID) and an INSendMessageIntent (conversation ID the room ID; in a group the group name as speakableGroupName and the group photo), donates it as an incoming INInteraction, and shows content.updating(from:). It needs the app entitlement com.apple.developer.usernotifications.communication, which testflight.yml adds only when the repository variable BIPE_COMM_NOTIFICATIONS is true, after the owner turns the capability on for the app ID. Without it, or with preview off for the account, the notification stays as before. Android: the sender Person carries the avatar as its icon and the Matrix ID as its key; each message notification has the shortcut ID of a long-lived conversation shortcut for the chat (the share-to-chat shortcut ID), so Android lists the chat under Conversations and allows priority and bubbles per person.

Kinds inviteJoined and groupLinkJoined (bipe-chat/bipe#967): bipe-api sends them through Sygnal like deviceApproval, with bipe_push_kind invite_joined or group_link_joined in the default_payload and the fixed event_id $invite_joined or $group_link_joined, without room_id and without content (no name, no handle). invite_joined goes to every Bipe Next pusher of the inviter when a person signs up with the inviter's personal invite (not a company account, not an admin invite) and the inviter's notification-prefs invite_joined is true. group_link_joined goes to every Bipe Next pusher of the link's creator when POST /v1/group-links/{code}/join invites a person who was not a member, or a sign-up with the link's code gets the invite, and the creator's group_link_joined pref is true; its default_payload also carries bipe_room_id, the group. The phone resolves account_route as for any push. inviteJoined: title bipe_invite_joined_push_title, body bipe_invite_joined_push_body; tap opens the owner account and runs invites refresh at once (the joined notice and the inviter's note, ADR 0136). groupLinkJoined: title bipe_group_link_joined_push_title, body bipe_group_link_joined_push_body; tap opens the owner account and the joined group bipe_room_id, else the conversation list. When inviteJoined arrives while the app is open, the app runs invites refresh at once and shows no banner (the joined notice covers it). Sound as for deviceApproval. An unknown or missing route shows nothing. No reply or mark-read action.

Kinds of the business tools (bipe-chat/bipe#320, ADR 0102): bipe-api sends them through Sygnal like deviceApproval, with the fixed event_id $<kind>, without room_id and without content (no business name, no service, no time). Customer: booking_tomorrow, booking_soon, booking_changed, order_updated, queue_called. Company account: work_new_booking, work_new_order, work_cancelled, work_today. The phone shows fixed text from these strings. A tap opens the account. A web customer gets no push.
